stem: A 14-year-old has no trusted adult outside the immediate family, feels school is pointless, has dropped all outside activities, and says, "Nothing I do changes anything". What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Several resilience supports are missing and protective factors should be actively reviewed
The history is reassuring because independence is increasing
The main issue is only a normal wish for privacy
The pattern mainly suggests advanced cognitive maturity
The history is normal if the adolescent has no major medical condition

explanation: Several resilience supports are missing, so protective factors should be actively reviewed. This pattern shows loss of a trusted adult, school connection, activities, social support, and an internal sense of control, which warrants follow-up rather than reassurance.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: The vignette removes multiple protective factors that usually support adolescent resilience. This should prompt active review of supports and strengths, not normalisation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the adolescent lacks several key protective factors, including trusted adult support, school engagement, outside activities, and a sense of agency.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because reduced connection and hopelessness are not reassuring signs of healthy independence.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the pattern is broader than privacy and includes loss of supports and hopeless statements.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the history does not indicate advanced maturity; it suggests reduced resilience supports.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the absence of major medical illness does not make the psychosocial risk profile normal.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
